cards.text: Israel is getting organized to serve at the house of the LORD. Now the list comes to the divisions of the gatekeepers, the men who guard the gates. First up, from the Korahites: Meshelemiah son of Kore.

Then the list runs through the families of Meshelemiah, Obed-edom and Hosah, and Obed-edom has eight sons, because God had blessed Obed-edom. His family alone comes to 62 capable men, and friend, I spent half my life catching SIX little cookie cutters at the edge of the counter!
All these gatekeeper divisions have duties ministering in the house of the LORD, just as their relatives did. Now they need to sort out who guards which gate.

cards.question: The gatekeepers need to decide who guards which gate. How do they decide?

answers.text: They cast lots for each gate

cards.question: When the lots are cast for the gates, who gets a turn?

cards.text: The lot for the East Gate falls to Shelemiah.

cards.question: Then lots are cast for Shelemiah's son Zechariah, a wise counselor. Which gate does his lot fall on?
Obed-edom draws the South Gate, and his sons draw the North Gate.

cards.text: Obed-edom's sons get the storehouses. Then the West Gate and the Shallecheth Gate on the ascending highway go to Shuppim and Hosah.

cards.question: Every gate now has its gatekeepers. When are guards stationed at them?

cards.text: Each day, Levites stand guard all around, from six on the east to two pairs at the storehouse to four at the highway on the west. Every post, every day, which means NOBODY on this crew gets to hit snooze.

cards.question: All these gatekeeper divisions come from the descendants of which two men?

cards.text: The gates are covered. But the house of God has more than doors to look after, and now their fellow Levites get a different job.

cards.question: What are these fellow Levites put in charge of at the house of God?

cards.text: From Ladan's family, Jehieli and his sons look after the treasuries of the house of the LORD. Then comes the officer in charge of the treasuries, Shebuel, and his family tree has a BIG name in it.

cards.question: Shebuel, the officer in charge of the treasuries, is a descendant of Moses.

cards.text: Shebuel's relative Shelomith and his brothers look after the treasuries of things dedicated by King David and his commanders. Friend, I spent years guarding a takeout menu in a junk drawer, and Shelomith is guarding gifts from a KING.

cards.question: Where did some of those things dedicated by David and his commanders come from?
Some of that battle plunder was dedicated to the repair of the house of the LORD.

cards.text: And these treasuries go WAY back. Even Samuel the seer, the prophet who anointed David (1 Samuel 16:13), dedicated things that are kept here.

cards.question: Which king of Israel (1 Samuel 11:15) also has dedicated things kept in the care of Shelomith and his brothers?

cards.text: Abner son of Ner, Saul's army commander (1 Samuel 14:50), is on the list, and so is Joab son of Zeruiah, David's army commander (2 Samuel 8:16). Everything dedicated sits under the care of Shelomith and his brothers.
Not every Levite here works inside the house of God. From the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons get the outside duties.

cards.question: Chenaniah and his sons have outside duties as ___ and ___ over Israel

cards.text: From the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his relatives step up for all the work of the LORD and the service of the king. That's 1,700 capable men, and I used to think six cookie cutters on one counter was a CROWD.

cards.question: Hashabiah's 1,700 men are put in charge of the affairs of Israel ___ of the Jordan

cards.text: Jerijah is chief of the Hebronites. Then, in the fortieth year of David's reign, strong, capable men are found among the Hebronites at Jazer in Gilead.

cards.question: In the fortieth year of David's reign, how are those strong capable men at Jazer in Gilead found?

cards.text: Jerijah's relatives come to 2,700 capable men, all heads of families. King David puts them over the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

cards.question: Jerijah's 2,700 men handle the affairs of the king, but none of the matters pertaining to God.

findings.problem: The opening line 'Israel is getting organized to serve at the house of the LORD' states a Bible fact from outside this passage (the surrounding chapters) with no reference.

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: Shelemiah shows up with no word on who he is. The baker has only met Meshelemiah (card 1), and the text clearly implies they are the same man, since his son Zechariah matches Meshelemiah's firstborn in 26:2. As written, the baker meets a new name with no context.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Card 1 already said the gatekeeper list starts 'from the Korahites.' Only one answer contains Korah, so the earlier setup rules out both wrong answers before the baker reasons about Merari.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Five of the stop's six choice cards are multiple choice (cards 4, 5, 7, 10, 12). There is one true or false and no fill in the blank, so one type dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Several story cards are bare retellings with no trace of Papa Dorin's voice. Stop 1 card 6 is a single flat sentence. Stop 2 cards 10, 15 and 17 read like a list. Across 32 verses there are only four jokes.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The card says the things were 'dedicated by King David and his commanders.' The text says they were dedicated by David, 'by the heads of families who were the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and by the army commanders' (26:26). It never calls them David's commanders. Card 6 repeats 'David and his commanders.'

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The joke 'I spent years guarding a takeout menu in a junk drawer' adds something new to his backstory. He never guarded anything in the drawer. The joke also breaks the comparison logic, because the action (guarding treasure) never happened in his story.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Gifts from other kings' is arguable. Elsewhere, David dedicated the articles King Toi sent him to the LORD (2 Samuel 8:10-11; 1 Chronicles 18:10-11), so a baker who knows the Bible could argue it is right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: Both blank orders make equal sense: 'officers and judges' and 'judges and officers.' A baker who reasons out the meaning but swaps the two words is marked wrong, so the card tests BSB word order instead of meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'south' (of the Jordan) doesn't fit. The Jordan runs north to south, so the land lies east or west of it, and 'south' stands out as an odd choice next to 'west' and 'east.'

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: 'Jerijah is chief of the Hebronites. Then, in the fortieth year...' adds a sequence the text doesn't give. Verse 31 doesn't say the records search came after Jerijah became chief.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Nearly this whole passage is lists: names, counts, gate assignments by lot (26:14-16), guard counts and regional assignments (26:30-32). The walkthrough treats 26:2-11, 17-18 and 21-25 as long stretches but asks choice cards on the gate-by-gate lot results (stop 1 cards 7, 8) and the regional assignments (stop 2 card 14), which are arguably 'mostly detail and not much happens.'
findings.question: When an entire passage is list material, which parts count as long stretches with no choice cards? Should details like which gate each man drew, or which side of the Jordan Hashabiah oversaw, get choice cards, or only the few things that carry meaning (lots for young and old alike, plunder dedicated to the house of the LORD, service for God and the king)?
